In the most recent organization chart, responsable EoR principal and responsable EoR alterno are both shown as the EOR. To prevent the potential for inadvertent communications, the TRP recommends that one person be identified as the EOR and the other person designated as the Alternate EOR. The Alternate EOR becomes the primary contact only when the EOR is unavailable.
An update of el panel técnico's outstanding recommendations from 2016 to 2018 was not provided at the April 2021 meeting. el panel técnico requests an update at the next meeting.

The EOR's 2020 DSI report (dated April 2020) included a backward looking review of the available flood storage based on bathymetry data gathered on December 2019, June 2020 and December 2020. In all cases, the available freeboards and beach widths under the IDF (i.e. PMF) were found to be LESS than design criteria. Particularly concerning is the fact that this deficiency occurred during a prolonged drought period, which could be exacerbated once the weather, and therefore, the operating pond volume, returns to normal. The condition described above represents a critical dam safety deficiency that must be rectified as soon as possible. Addressing this deficiency is intricately linked to TRP Recommendations #2021-4, #2021-5, #2021-6 and #2021-7, as outlined below.

nombre: Quantifiable Performance Objectives (QPOs) for Flood Management and TARP
descripcion: The flood management deficiency discussed in TRP Recommendation #2021-3 was identified in hindsight, based on a review of the previous year's bathymetry, and apparently did not trigger any alarms to notify the EOR nor the Tailings Superintendent of this deficiency. el panel técnico recommends that the EOR identify appropriate Quantifiable Performance Objectives (QPOs) that are relevant to flood management (e.g. operating pond volume, freeboard, beach width, etc.), and establish thresholds for those QPOs in the TSF's Trigger Action Response Plan (TARP).

nombre: Execution Plan for Effective Implementation of Master Tailings Deposition Plan
descripcion: It has been evident (see TRP Recommendation #2020-14) that there is a shortfall in sand production which, in part, has contributed to the delay in completing the Dam Recovery Plan and, therefore, the delay in resuming conventional hydraulic construction using the spigot method. Shimin InGenieria has completed a study (dated Dec. 31, 2020) providing recommendations to improve the tailings deposition system to provide extra flexibility. In addition, the EOR has recommended that the Master Tailings Deposition Plan should be updated to reflect the current operating conditions and enforce a more stringent monitoring and recording process for the tailings tonnages and their distribution. el panel técnico concurs with the above referenced recommendations. However, el panel técnico also recommends the following: a) The recommendations by Shamin InGeniera for improvements to the tailings deposition system should be incorporated into the updated Master Plan taking into consideration the expected schedule for implementing those recommendations. b) A detailed Execution Plan should be developed that clearly outlines how the updated Master Plan will be effectively and practically implemented and clearly identify who is responsible for each activity. The Execution Plan should incorporate TRP Recommendation #2021-7 as outlined below.

nombre: TSF Water Balance Model Responsibility and implementation
descripcion: Previous TRP Recommendation #2016-23 recommended that a water balance model be developed for the TSF. This work was reported to be complete in November 2018. In the recent 2020 DSI report, the EOR identified numerous data gaps in the existing water balance model. Given these data gaps, and because of the importance of the water balance model in relation to tailings deposition (TRP Recommendation #2021-4) and flood management (TRP Recommendation #2021-3), el panel técnico recommends that the responsibility for maintaining the TSF water balance should be assigned to a single qualified individual. Key tasks of that individual should include: a) address the data gaps identified by the EOR in the 2020 DSI report as a matter of urgency b) Developing a comprehensive data collection of all inflow and outflow parameters including hydrogeological influences c) Carry out monthly (minimum) reconciliations to d) Regular updating of the water balance model data collection program and reconciliatory validations of the model The updated water balance model should be used as a tool to forecast future pond levels to ensure operating and flood storage requirements are always maintained.

It is apparent that there are still some major challenges associated with the Cordillera TSF operations. The compounding effects of several factors (prolonged dam recovery program, sand shortfall, prolonged drought conditions, complexity of operations, civil unrest in 2019, the Covid pandemic starting in 2020, shortage of operating staff, etc.) have led to the current condition where the TSF appears to have little to no Going forward there is a need to closely integrate the results of various activities that impact safe operations of the TSF. In particular el panel técnico recommends that the overall strategy for operating the TSF must be developed that closely integrates the results of the following: a) Mine plan b) Flood management plan (TRP Recommendation #2016-13 #2021-3 & c) Water balance model (TRP Recommendation #2016-23 and #2021-6) d) Drought plan (TRP Recommendation #2020-4) e) Beach width development plan (TRP Recommendation #2016-17 #2018-8 and #2018-9) f) Staffing plan (TRP Recommendation #2017-1j and #2020-6) g) Execution plan for the Master Tailings Deposition Plan (TRP Recommendation #2021-5) Sensitivity analysis should also be conducted to consider potential impacts if improvement projects for the tailings deposition system are delayed and identify corresponding contingency plans as required.

The TRP noted that the technical memorandum did not provide any details on the key assumptions, method of dynamic analyses, basis of the material parameter selections or how the uncertainties were accounted for. In addition, the deformations were only described as qualitatively as “large”, but the magnitudes and overall pattern of the “large deformations” were not reported. The TRP recommended that additional information be provided for review.

el consorcio plans to integrate all TSF operation activities under the responsibility of a single contractor. Specific details and terms of reference for the Contractor were not provided, and are still under development. el panel técnico looks forward to further details as they become available. At this stage, el panel técnico offers the following comments and recommendations: a) The proposed approach must consider measures to deal with factors that are beyond the control of el consorcio and/or the contractor such as copper prices drought or extreme wet conditions large earthquakes etc. b) The terms of reference must clearly outline the KPIs that have dam safety targets and regulatory compliance (e.g. freeboard beach width limit equilibrium factors of safety groundwater and surface water quality etc.) as well as dam safety responsibilities and accountabilities (Contractor el consorcio Tailings Superintendent EOR c) This integration project represents another major challenge to the TSF operations on top of the existing major challenges that are still being addressed (per TRP Recommendations #2021-3 to #2021-9 inclusive). The potential implications associated with this added complication must be carefully reviewed by AAC and the EOR.

nombre: Categorizing DSI Report Recommendations by the EOR
descripcion: The 2020 DSI report by the EOR contains quite a large number of recommendations. To facilitate clarity, el panel técnico recommends that the DSI recommendations be grouped into various key categories a) dam safety deficiencies b) regulatory non-compliance c) OMS related issues d) QA/QC related issues e) etc. It is likely that categorizing the recommendations in the above manner would have more easily highlighted/elevated the dam safety deficiency in terms of flood management as described in TRP Recommendation #2021-3.

TRP Recommendation #2016-24 had recommended that the potential for geochemical clogging of the drains for all dams should be examined. This work was reportedly completed as of June 15, 2020. During the April 2021 TRP meetings, el panel técnico was advised that the main finger drain at the West Dam was found to be clogged with fines. This was attributed to erosion damage/surface runoff which transported fines to the drains. However, reddish brown discolored water and coated drain materials were observed, which indicate a potential for activity of slime-forming bacteria in the seepage water. Moreover, the 2020 DSI report by the EOR recorded observations of a) The occurrence of b) Seepage water from the drains should collected and its chemistry analyzed for major ions and trace metals such as Fe Mn. c) The pH of the seepage water should be monitored at the collection chamber. d) The observations and results of the chemical analyses should be used to further review the potential for drain clogging and to update the previously completed study.

nombre: Main Dam - Design Modifications on Left Abutment
descripcion: Tailings deposition on the left abutment has already encroached into the upstream footprint area of the Main Dam. Shifting the dam centreline further downstream is not possible because of the constraint imposed by the existing property limit. Therefore, continuing with the downstream-method-of-construction on the left abutment cannot be carried out. The project team has proposed an alternate option whereby the portion of the Main Dam on the left abutment is changed to a centreline construction methodology. The project team acknowledges this will require a permit amendment. The TRP concurs with the project team' 1. Time is of the essence and it is critical that construction of an upstream “containment dam” is carried out as soon as possible to prevent tailings deposition from encroaching further into the upstream dam footprint area. 2. To minimize the impact associated with difference in stiffness between the downstream constructed dam and the centreline construction dam we suggest that the portion of the dam section between the “containment dam” and the Main Dam centreline should comprise compacted cyclone sand hydraulically placed and compacted in cells (i.e. paddock construction). The width of the upstream compacted cyclone sand zone should progressively increase from the “containment dam” location to the downstream constructed Main Dam section. This concept is schematically shown in Figure 4.12 in the main report. 3. It is emphasized that the centreline-method-of-construction will necessarily require closer integration with the tailings deposition plan. This requirement must be clearly communicated to the operations team and documented in the OMS Manual. 4. While the current property limit represents a hard boundary now el consorcio minero should apply a concerted effort to pursue the possibility of accessing more land beyond the property limit. Having access to more land beyond the property limit provides greater flexibility for modifying/improving the dam design in the future in the event adverse conditions are detected. 5. Finally the EOR for Cordillera is la EoR and their approval and acceptance of the final design on the left abutment is required. It will be important for the EOR to conduct an assessment of the proposed changes on the left abutment as soon as practical so that any additional measures that could be required to ensure ongoing satisfactory performance of the Main Dam are identified and timely implemented. el consorcio (2021b) requiere que el memorando de criterios de diseño esté actualizado y utilizado como parte de los controles clave para una operación segura. El último memorándum de criterios de diseño fue preparado por el EOR (la EoR 2017). El memorando debe actualizarse para reflejar actualizaciones de diseño recientes según lo requerido por los estándares el consorcio (2021B).

Documentation of the classifications does not include mention of what information the assessment was based on, nor does it include a complete description of the specific consequences that the evaluation team envisioned. The Plant Dam received a low rating in some of the classification categories, suggesting that the team used some information other than the la consultora geotécnica (2020) inundation study. It is recommended that el consorcio expand their consequence classification template to include: including the basis for each loss estimate a flood-induced failure or both.

The la consultora geotécnica (2019) dambreach inundation study was completed before the CDA (2021) guidelines were issued, so the criteria and some of the information used in this DSR to assess the study were not available at the time of the work. Revisions to the dambreach analysis are highly unlikely to change the consequence classification of Cordillera. However, the comparison of the la consultora geotécnica (2020) work with current guidelines raises some concerns for emergency response plans. It is recommended that: The inundation modelling should be extended further downstream. Initial downstream conditions should be selected to be consistent with the assumed failure scenario. Until these issues are resolved emergency plans should be annotated to indicate that the potential inundation extents for flood-induced failure scenarios may be underestimated. The next dam breach assessment should consider both the water / tailings fluid (Process I) and liquefied tailings releases (Process II) when analyzing a flood-induced failure.

AA’s freeboard criteria are not clearly documented in the OMS manual (el consultor externo 2020b), as the criteria changed after the manual was produced. Changes to tailings deposition to meet the current criteria are ongoing, but it is understood that el consorcio staff are reluctant to incorporate the current freeboard objective into the OMS manual because it will take some time (multiple years) before the objective can be achieved. However, from a dam safety perspective, the criteria should be documented as an operational goal with an acknowledgement that they cannot yet be met, rather than using unclear or out of date documentation. It is recommended that: The minimum beach width required during the IDF be established A well-conceived plan towards meeting the freeboard requirements in a timely manner be developed and incorporated into the tailings deposition and dam raising plan. TRP21-05 TRP General Historical Freeboard The Technical Review Panel (TRP) identified the lack of flood storage as a critical dam safety deficiency (el panel técnico 2021). The fact that apparently no alarms were triggered by the insufficient storage was also identified as a serious issue. The provided data did not include crest elevations for the Plant Dam. The Plant Dam as well as the 5 m specified freeboard there should be included in pond and dam crest elevation reporting immediately.

As an urgent priority, el consorcio debería update their freeboard management and surveillance systems to address the fact that the freeboard as currently managed does not meet either the design intent (la EoR 2017) or good practice as prescribed in the CDA (2013) guidelines. The system should include the following elements: 1. The beach width required during the IDF should be determined based on geotechnical considerations. 2. The two components of freeboard (A - flood storage below the beach plus the height of the specified beach width and B - a height above the beach contact based on regulatory requirements that includes an allowance for wave runup and seismic settlement) should be clearly identified in the OMS manual. 3. The IDF surcharge allowance should be updated regularly (at least once per quarter) accounting for changes in the stage-storage curve as the tailings surface changes to ensure that adequate freeboard is provided throughout the life of the MRF. It is understood that el consorcio is currently re-evaluating the IDF surcharge allowance monthly (Tim Gardner el consorcio 2022 pers. comm.). 4. Routine reporting of pond and dam crest levels (like that shown on Figure 6.1) should be updated to include: a. The height of the IDF flood surcharge plus the height of the required beach during the IDF (Freeboard Component A) b. The elevation of the beach contact at each dam c. The 3 m regulatory allowance above the beach contact (Freeboard Component B) d. The crest elevation and 5 m freeboard allowance at the Plant Dam e. The South Dam and Southwest Dam crest and beach contact elevations as soon as construction begins on those structures.

Based on CDA (2013) guidelines, the 3 m regulatory allowance above the beach contact is extremely conservative if the IDF is contained below that line. From a dam safety perspective, it is more important to contain the IDF and to maintain an appropriate beach width below the beach contact elevation (Component A) than to meet the regulatory allowance above the beach contact elevation (Component B). It is recommended that: - el consorcio debería prioritize dam safety (Component A of the freeboard) over regulatory compliance (Component B). el consorcio debería discuss the freeboard issue with the regulators and attempt to obtain a relaxation of the 3 m requirement for Component B while el consorcio focusse el consorcio debería consider other actions to improve dam safety such as improving the lining of the pond to increase safe flood storage capacity and/or constructing a spillway.

Several design documents were reviewed (e.g., la EoR 2021b) and consistently did not include detailed and up-to-date documentation supporting the development of the geology model, design assumptions and material characterization. el panel técnico recommends that el consorcio maintain an up-to-date Design Basis Report (DBR) that includes up-to-date references used to inform the design. This report is consistent with the GISTM (2020) standards. Alternatively, the design criteria memorandum by la EoR (2017) may be updated to meet the DBR objectives as outline by the GISTM (2020) standards.

The FMEA included an assessment of four failure modes (overtopping, slope instability, foundation failure, and internal erosion), potential causes, potential consequences and existing control measures. To improve effectiveness and meet the objectives of the FMEA, el panel técnico recommends expanding the FMEA to include documentation of the participating individuals/disciplines, event tree, and risk assessment.

la EoR identified loose cyclone sand zones based on CPTu programs that were conducted in 2018 and 2019 and concluded that the FOS criteria was met based on the analyses completed for current dam elevations (Crest elevation was 727 m for the Main Dam), despite the presence of the loose cyclone sand zones because these zones are not currently saturated. However, it is not clear if this will be the case at the ultimate design elevation where portions of the loose sand may become saturated. Stability assessment should be undertaken for the ultimate design elevation to check if the FOS criteria will be met with the presence of contractive cyclone sand that may become saturated. Sensitivity analyses should be undertaken to encompass the range of uncertainties (e.g., saturation and loose zones).

The static cases were modelled with materials using drained strengths parameters. This may be appropriate for dilative materials such as compacted cyclone sands. However, contractive materials such as slimes, loose cyclone sand (if present), and high plasticity clay foundation could fail in an undrained manner under static conditions. More specifically the Main Dam foundation (Unit 1) includes sands clays from alluvial fluvial and colluvial origin. The East Dam foundation includes heavily weathered volcanic rock (residual soil) and high plasticity clay units. el panel técnico recommends that peak undrained strengths should be considered for potentially contractive tailings and foundations units in the static case and residual undrained strengths for strain weakening (where applicable) should be considered for the post-earthquake case. Using these recommended strength parameters will lead to a lower FOS compared to that reported by la EoR 2016b. The stability analyses shall be revised for all the containment dams accordingly to assess if the FOS meets the design criteria outlined by the EOR and included in the regulatory approval for Cordillera MRF. TRP21-08 DSR General Slope Inestability The cyclones and dams have recently been raised using the paddock construction method which has raised concerns with the TRP relating to highly variable conditions with large fill interfaces between paddocks where compaction could be compromised. To verify compaction, the EOR advised that a program of shallow test pits ranging between 4 m to 5 m were carried out. The TRP noted that regardless of the density results, backfilling the test pits would be challenging given the restricted working area in the test pits (el panel técnico 2021). el panel técnico recommends that a regularly scheduled CPT program is undertaken all three-cyclone sand constructed dams (Main, West and East) verify the compaction specifications are satisfied.

The West Dam includes claystone that is described to be weathered at the surface. It is not clear if the weathered zones may exhibit undrained behaviour. It is also unclear if la EoR had assessed the material for the possibility of slickensides or strain weakening behaviour for the intact claystone. el panel técnico recommends that these considerations should be discussed as part of the material characterization for the Cordillera dam design.

50% of the PGA, resulting in approximately 0.45g. la EoR (2016b) used the recommended seismic hazard coefficient recommended by the 2006 seismic hazard study leading to 0.17g, much lower than expected. el panel técnico recommends that the horizontal seismic coefficient be reviewed.

Typical failure modes considered by la EoR are shown in Figure 6.4 and Figure 6.5. el panel técnico recommends that additional failure modes that are shown on Figure 6.6 to Figure 6.10, and discussed in Table 6.4 and Table 6.5, should also be considered.

Only one earthquake record was used in the analysis while it is typical to include more earthquake records than this (e.g., at least 7). The earthquake time history used in the analysis appears to be based on a seismic hazard study completed by la EoR in 2019, however there is a more recent seismic hazard study completed by la consultora geotécnica (2020). It is unclear why the more recent study was not used for la EoR’ (2021i) dynamic assessment since it was available at the time. The la consultora geotécnica study (la consultora geotécnica 2020) identifies subduction and crustal seismic sources for the MCE. These events have different frequency contents and durations, meaning that either of them could be critical to the dam performance. el panel técnico recommends that the deformation assessment be expanded to include the sources and time histories that were documented in la consultora geotécnica (2020), aligning the work with international practice.

The Mohr-Coulomb constitutive model was applied to all soil units and does not account for cyclic softening or post-cyclic strength loss. There is insufficient characterization data presented in la EoR (2021i) to determine if this is appropriate consider the potential for weaker layers in the weathered tuff and alluvial, colluvial and fluvial layers. Additional characterization of these units should be considered.

With high seismic loading at this site, it would be typical to have a detailed characterization of the soil foundation units, including CPT data, vane shear data, sampling and static and cyclic laboratory testing. The constitutive models would then typically be calibrated to the behaviour seen in these tests. It is possible that some of this characterization was completed in a referenced report in the deformation analysis, however there were no calibration results presented in la EoR (2021i). If a detailed characterization and calibration has not been completed, el panel técnico recommends that this work is undertaken. If calibration has been completed, details of it should be presented in la EoR (2021i).

Large displacements have been calculated for the West Dam and East Dam. The implications of these displacements appear to have been used to conclude that they would not impact the overall integrity of the dam. A more formal process to assess the potential implications of these displacements leading to failure modes such as overtopping (e.g., considering different potential water levels at the time of the displacements) or potential secondary failure mechanism (e.g., post-cyclic strength loss or unravelling from the initial failures) should be completed. Given that these displacements are extensive, the potential impact of aftershocks should be considered.

The instrumentation network does not include inclinometers to monitor horizontal deformation within the dam fill and foundation units. This observation/recommendation was also made by the TRP since 2016. el panel técnico recommends installing additional inclinometers.

It appears that no piezometers are installed in the foundation units to verify the inherent design assumption that there is no excess pore pressure in the foundation units. We recommend that el consorcio debería consider installing foundation piezometers, especially within the clay foundation units. We also recommend installing piezometers in the coarse foundation units to monitor for artesian conditions that may develop.

Based on the measured phreatic surface shown on Figure 6.3, most of the vibrating wire piezometers installed in the cyclone dam fill are dry. While this may be interpreted as a favourable condition, these piezometers are likely severely de-saturated and may take long time to become re-saturated and accurately measure pore pressure, should the phreatic surface rise. We recommend that el consorcio debería consider assessing the functionality of the dry piezometers and augment the instrumentation network with standpipe piezometers.

A draft RASCI (Responsible, Accountable, Supporting, Consulted, Informed) matrix was presented during the interview which appeared to provide sufficient details regarding roles and responsibilities. el panel técnico recommends that the RASCI should be finalized and incorporated in the OMS manual.

Based on interview feedback, the EOR is not engaged in the planning and operation of the MRF as required by el consorcio standards. el panel técnico recommends that the roles and responsibilities of the EOR, as set out by el consorcio (2021b,c) standards, are adhered to by the operations staff. The RASCI that is currently in development should help address this shortcoming in EOR engagement.

No evidence was provided during staff interviews to demonstrate that a formal Management of Change (MOC) process has been implemented for managing changes related to design, construction, and operation for the Cordillera MRF. As an example – It was found that a significant change, related to the delaying of the relocation of the cyclone plant adjacent to the dam abutment, was not formally documented. The change will require modifications to the MRF, specifically a permanent flood barrier will be required to be constructed around the cyclone plant (Figure 7.2). This is a significant change (with potential impact on dam safety) that should have been formally documented using MOC process. We recommend that el consorcio debería develop and deploy dam safety training for staff in key dam safety roles and cover key processes including MOC and Risk Assessment. We also recommend implementation of the MOC procedure to the cyclone plant and all future changes relating to the MRF that are planned or in progress.

nombre: Emergency Preparedness and Emergency Response Plans
descripcion: The pre-defined actions in the ERP do not include sufficient details to support timely response in case of an emergency. For example, the action plan for responding to high seepage flow observation does not include sufficient details about filter material source, specification, and filter installation procedures. We recommend including greater level of details to facilitate timely response in case of an emergency.

nombre: Emergency Preparedness and Emergency Response Plans
descripcion: The ERP is limited to planning for emergencies that are contained within the site and do not involve dam breach (e.g., cracking, surface erosion, seepage, etc.). This limitation in the ERP present inconsistency with the el consorcio (2021c) expectations. We recommend expanding the scope of the ERP to include emergencies that involve tailings run out for completeness and compliance with the el consorcio (2021c) standards and accepted industry practice.

nombre: Emergency Preparedness and Emergency Response Plans
descripcion: Contact lists for both ERP and EPP have not been updated since 2020. The ERP should be updated or linked to a live directory to ensure effective communication in case of an emergency.

Asegúrese de que haya recursos adecuados disponibles para respaldar el CP, dada la complejidad de la operación de Vicuña, que incluyen: - Gestión de proyectos de capital complejos (por ejemplo actualización de la planta de ciclones).

Asegúrese de que haya recursos adecuados disponibles para apoyar al equipo EOR cumplir su papel crítico de seguridad de dama y aclarar el papel de los otros consultores (la consultora geotécnica, el consultor externo, el consultor externo y otros) que realizan tareas de diseño importantes. El EOR no está suficientemente involucrado en la planificación, diseño y operación del MRF. Esta preocupación había sido identificada en el DSR (consulte la recomendación DSR22-LT-28) donde se atribuyó a la falta de claridad sobre los roles y la responsabilidad. Desde que se hicieron las recomendaciones de DSR, se han descrito el rol y las responsabilidades y se ha desarrollado la matriz de Rasci. Sin embargo, las asignaciones de diseño clave aún no están lideradas por el EOR y no parecen caer bajo la responsabilidad del EOR (por ejemplo, caracterización del material y diseño final de la presa).

El TRP observó dificultades para encontrar documentación relevante/actualizada del proyecto. Esto da como resultado ineficiencias durante la revisión y también puede dar lugar a pérdidas de datos y/o duplicación de esfuerzo. El TRP recomienda que el consorcio minero (AA) considere desarrollar un sistema de gestión de la información para beneficiarse completamente de la inversión de el consorcio en creación de datos y servicios de ingeniería.

La construcción de espigones de tubería en la playa blanda puede presentar un riesgo potencial para el personal si la playa licúa. Considere eliminar los terraplenes cuando sea posible (por ejemplo, East Dam) o desarrollar procedimientos operativos seguros y plan de respuesta de emergencia para garantizar la seguridad del personal (por ejemplo, la presa oeste).

Major remediation work is being undertaken at the Plant Dam that requires excavation of the dam fill at its left and right abutments without MOC. The TRP recommends the following: - Develop and deploy dam safety training for staff in key supervisory roles (Superintendent SIB Project Manager Operations Manager and EOR) including familiarization with standard requirements Similar observation/recommendation was made in the DSR (DSR22-LT-29).

Nonlinear deformation analysis can provide important insights, but it depends greatly on the: Input earthquake motions, Phreatic surface, Soil strength characterization, Soil response model and its calibration, and Numerical simulations of the tailings storage facility as a system. The TRP recommends the following: - Use robust nonlinear effective stress soil model(s) (e.g. PM4Sand) - Calibrate analyses with monitoring data (e.g. EQ records piezometers and inclinometers) - Use at least 7 EQ ground motion records in the assessment. Additionally the deformation analyses must consider the contribution volumetric strains (i.e. post-liquefaction volumetric-induced ground deformations).

La fuerza residual de los relaves licuados debe estimarse en función de los resultados de las pruebas in situ y de laboratorio. Considere la oportunidad de evaluar las características de las partículas de arena de relaves con imágenes de microscopio electrónico de barrido.

Without sufficient geologic data, large uncertainties remain on factors that can affect the performance of the tailings storage facility. There is uncertainty of the characteristics of soft rock and hard rock units and the overall rock structure (i.e., folds and faults), insufficient data to evaluate if continuous clay layers exist below the dam, unclear if potentially expansive clay zones exist, the potential for increased seepage due to the rock under the dam being more fissured as the dam is raised, and the poorly understood activity and characteristics of the Esmeralda fault and micro-seismicity. Invest in additional geologic characterization to reduce uncertainty.
The use of the criterion of zones with displacement > 2% of the total displacement to identify sliding zones is not defined clearly and not justified sufficiently.

Design, performance, and risk management details were insufficient for the TRP to review during its visit in December 2022. A follow-up virtual meeting in January 2023 provided additional details but it was still difficult for the TRP to understand fully key details of important design and performance issues in the summary slides presented. Additional TRP recommendations may be developed after review of additional materials. Future TRP presentations should include sufficient details such as material characterization key design assumptions references etc. Also insufficient details were provided about the status of the previous TRP recommendation. Provide an action plan for the TRP recommendations from 2016 to 2020.

Many of the findings of the TRP visit in December 2022 duplicate observations and recommendations developed in the el panel técnico (2022) Dam Safety Review. Hence, they are not repeated in this list of 2023 TRP recommendations. Additionally, some critical topics were not discussed during the 2023 TRP visit, such as dam breach analysis. 2022 DSR recommendations scored as Critical (5) or Important (4) should be addressed concurrently while responding to the 2023 TRP recommendations.

Hydraulic calculation report PLB-037-4830-HE-0002 Rev1 (Shimin 2021) for the new main dam cyclone facility is based on pumping a 66% wt. solids (wt. solids/wt. solids + wt. water) sand underflow tailings slurry to the embankment. la operación reported a 75 % wt. solids sand underflow tailings slurry is needed to avoid erosion of the downstream face of the dam. At 75% wt. solids there is a risk pumping distance may need to be limited across the dam crest. el panel técnico recommends el consorcio align the process design with the operational requirements for dam construction.

No rheology tests were completed to design the sand underflow tailings delivery pumping system. el panel técnico recommends el consorcio check why these tests were not completed in particular considering the higher concentration required by operations. Hydraulic sensitivity calculations of how rheology changes with increasing and decreasing changes in solids concentration is recommended to manage the respective pumping distance of systems. The review should use performance data of the operating tailings delivery system to confirm the result of the hydraulic calculations.
la operación does not have access to the cyclone simulations. Operations should have access to these simulations to effectively manage the set-up of the cyclones.

el panel técnico has not seen record of the fines placed in the embankment. We recommend that the EoR is provided with these records in order to confirm suitable material is placed during dam construction.

While el panel técnico was at site during the 2023 TRP, the west side cyclone facilities and pumps were not able to deliver sand across the main dam crest. el panel técnico recommends el consorcio revisit the staging of their infrastructure to avoid similar limitations in the future. This review should include the hydraulic limitation of the pumps in terms of dam crest elevation, pumping distance and %solids of the sand underflow slurry.

As the new cyclone plant comes into operation on the west side there may be an opportunity to use the existing pumping infrastructure on the east side for additional beach construction in front of the east dam. Beaching in front of the east dam would help keep the pond away from the dam. el panel técnico recommends a review of whether additional beaching volumes would be possible from the east side pumping facilities.

The TRP observed pressurized pipelines suspended on cables, which could result in significant damage to the dam slopes and crests if they were to rupture. the TRP recommends to complete a risk assessment identify critical controls and develop an emergency response plan.

The TRP observed steep slopes with visibly loose material at the abutments. with poor materials removed and high compaction effort of sand placed on foundation and rock face. - TRP recommends appropriate tie-in specifications be developed and included in the OMS and IFC drawings.

The TRP observed that the beach slope at the Main Dam is 0.3% and can be inundated by a small rise in the pond. - TRP recommends that tailings deposition strategies be developed to steepen the beach slope as per the design.

The TRP observed that current dam construction practice allows for slope steepening near the dam crest. and the maximum allowable height and slope angle be clearly defined to avoid these operational issues in the future.
The TRP recommends that the design for the ultimate dam height be updated to incorporate the changes in the material parameters and design basis.

The TRP recommends to conduct a Multicriteria Alternative Analysis (MAA) among the implementation of a flood spillway, Plant Dam crest growth, and the loss of water reservoir capacity in the TLT, including technical-economic, environmental, and legal aspects in tis evaluation. In the short term, advancing Plan Dam crest growth appears to be the most feasible alternative
The very flat beach will impact their ability to keep the pond away from the dams under flood storage conditions. The TRP recommends improved beaching practice to address this.

It is recommended to characterize the natural hill slopes along the tailings launder (and other linear conveying facilities) and implement reinforcements if needed and periodic inspections (to be included in the OMS).

The TRP recommends additional resources be devoted to the sulphate plume issue and supports efforts to try to secure permits from the appropriate regulatory agencies to enable effective mitigation measures of the sulphate plume to be carried out expeditiously.
The TRP recommends adding a well to intercept seepage in the right abutment of the main dam before it emerges as surface flow to eliminate surficial seepage.
The TRP recommends a hydrogeologist be added to the TRP as soon as possible.

nombre: Deficiencias en el sistema de control de compactación
descripcion: Se han observado deficiencias durante el proceso de control de compactación, las cuales la EoR ha mencionado en los distintos memorandum técnicos emitidos (PLB-12201181-RET-4850-CE-0056, PLB-12201181-RET-4850-CE-0057 y PLB-12201181-RET-4850-CE-0134)
Durante la realización de trabajos de restitución de talud en MP, se pasó a llevar piezómetro y en consecuencia, se dañó, dejando de registrar lecturas.
